items.q: In which demographic group is Hashimoto's thyroiditis most common?
items.exp: Under Hashimoto's Thyroiditis FEATURES: 'most common in middle-aged female'. (Book p906)

items.q: Match the immunogenetic associations of Hashimoto's thyroiditis — 1) HLA alleles 2) Immune checkpoint polymorphisms … A) HLA-DR3, DR4, DR5 (can be ANA positive) B) CTLA-4 and PTPN-22 polymorphisms
items.exp: HLA associations are DR-3 / DR-4 / DR5 (can be ANA +ve); non-HLA gene polymorphisms are CTLA-4 / PTPN-22. (Book p906)

items.q: Assess gland changes in Hashimoto's thyroiditis: I The thyroid gland is commonly not enlarged. II When goitre is present, it is characteristically an irregular, firm, heterogeneous, non-tender enlargement.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Gland changes: 'Commonly not enlarged' and 'If goitre present : Irregular/ firm/ heterogeneous non tender enlargement of gland'. (Book p906)

items.q: On gross examination of a resected thyroid from a middle-aged woman with autoimmune hypothyroidism, the gland appears fibrosed, pale, and firm. What accounts for the pale appearance?
opts: Diffuse fatty infiltration of stromal tissue
items.exp: Under Gross appearance: 'Fibrosed gland' and 'Pale gland d/t lymphoid infiltration'. (Book p906)

items.q: On microscopic examination of Hashimoto's thyroiditis, the prominent lymphocytic infiltration characteristically organizes into ___ formation.
items.exp: Microscopic appearance: 'Lymphocytic infiltration -> Germinal center formation'. (Book p906)

items.q: What are the transformed, hypereosinophilic epithelial cells with abundant granular cytoplasm seen in Hashimoto's thyroiditis called?
items.exp: Page 906 notes: 'Hypereosinophilic cells : Hürthle cells' and 'Oxyphilic metaplasia'. (Book p906)

items.q: Regarding the microscopic findings in Hashimoto's thyroiditis: I The follicular lumen characteristically shows an absence of colloid. II Oxyphilic metaplasia with Hürthle cells is a key hallmark.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Microscopic hallmarks on page 906 include: 'Absence of colloid' and 'Oxyphilic metaplasia' with Hürthle cells. (Book p906)

items.q: Which malignancy has the highest associated relative risk in patients with longstanding Hashimoto's thyroiditis?
opts: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma > papillary carcinoma thyroid
items.exp: Under Associated malignancy: 'Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma > papillary carcinoma thyroid'. (Book p906)

items.q: Match the malignancy associated with Hashimoto's thyroiditis to its relative frequency order — 1) Most strongly associated malignancy 2) Secondary associated thyroid carcinoma … A) Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma B) Papillary carcinoma thyroid
items.exp: Associated malignancy hierarchy: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma is more strongly associated than papillary carcinoma of thyroid. (Book p906)

items.q: The cellular and cytokine mediators driving thyroid destruction in Hashimoto's include T-cells (both CD-8 and ___), plasma cells, and the cytokine ___.
items.exp: Pathological mediators: 'T-cell (CD-8, CD-4)', 'IFN-gamma', and 'Plasma cell'. (Book p906)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed on page 906 as a histological feature or mediator of Hashimoto's thyroiditis?
opts: Abundant colloid retention in dilated follicles
Lymphocytic infiltration with germinal center formation
items.exp: In Hashimoto's, there is characteristically an 'Absence of colloid', not abundant colloid retention. (Book p906)

items.q: A 50-year-old woman with a 15-year history of Hashimoto's thyroiditis presents with a rapidly enlarging thyroid goiter. Biopsy demonstrates extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma. What is the classic risk hierarchy noted on page 906?
opts: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma > papillary carcinoma thyroid
Papillary carcinoma thyroid > follicular carcinoma thyroid
Medullary thyroid carcinoma > anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
Follicular thyroid carcinoma > marginal zone lymphoma
items.exp: Page 906 explicitly highlights: 'Associated malignancy : Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma > papillary carcinoma thyroid'. (Book p906)
